purpose: Current web-platform source check for rev0181 runtime-core storage reservation reconciliation and duplicate-hint cleanup. The findings keep the change conservative: browser storage estimates are advisory, queued/scheduled work can be aborted while pending, Web Lock request abort drops ungranted requests only, and BrowserRT should reconcile its own local reservation bookkeeping rather than claim durable browser quota reservation.

sources.label: MDN Storage quotas and eviction criteria
sources.finding: Browser storage quotas and eviction criteria differ by browser; data is normally per-origin, best-effort by default, and persistent storage is still a browser policy posture rather than a BrowserRT reservation.

sources.label: MDN AbortSignal
sources.finding: AbortSignal communicates cancellation to async operations, is worker-available, exposes aborted/reason, and already-aborted signals should cause abortable operations to reject immediately.

sources.label: MDN LockManager.request
sources.finding: A Web Lock request signal drops the request if not already granted; lock-stealing warns that previously running code continues, so queued cancellation must not be confused with cancelling already-running mutation.

sources.label: MDN Scheduler.postTask
sources.finding: postTask accepts an AbortSignal/TaskSignal and delayed tasks may be rejected with the abort reason, reinforcing the need for explicit pending-work cleanup.

appliedSpeculation: Because runtime-core exposes both the adapter and scheduler, consumer code can cancel adapter-owned queued work directly through the scheduler. Without reconciliation, the adapter can over-count stale pending put bytes and reject later safe work.

Duplicate-budget hints are intentionally narrow and safe, but stale hints after delete/cleanup are still observability debt and bounded memory waste; clearing them keeps duplicate accounting honest without trusting caller-supplied duplicate claims.
nonClaims: This research artifact is not a browser conformance test, cross-browser matrix, OPFS quota reservation proof, eviction survival proof, Web Lock fairness proof, or Storage Buckets implementation claim.
